transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sophie Park (CISO, Blackwill), Alan Rees (Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Legal), Tom Briggs (ML Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): discussion focused on data residency, logging constraints, encrypted at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM keys, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for financial-data workloads; next steps include artifact handoff and pilot scope.

Topics: data residency, HIPAA/GDPR overlap, SOC 2 evidence, log retention & redaction, VPC/private deployment, dedicated capacity SLAs, KV cache/prefix caching behavior, model fallbacks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining we have about 50 minutes on the agenda to walk residency and compliance fit for Redwood. quick intro from us, i'm maya, AE, and diego is our SE.
[00:14] Diego Alvarez: hi all, thanks, real quick i want to surface the big levers - hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), key management (customer KMS/HSM), and logging capture. we'll be pragmatic.
[00:30] Sophie Park: thanks. i'll kick off — our top-line is reg and audit readiness. we're an asset manager, so client PII and transaction traces must stay EU-only. so data residency and audit logs are the two big gates for us. also HIPAA overlap for a small line of business.
[00:48] Alan Rees: timeline: pilot in Q1, production later in Q2 if everything checks out. key stakeholders: security (Sophie), platform (me), legal (Priya), and ML team (Tom).
[01:05] Maya Chen: perfect. quick qual — are you okay with hosted if we can prove region-locking and no cross-border control plane access? or do you need Dedicated or Private from day one?
[01:20] Sophie Park: hosted is okay only if we get region lock, explicit audit lines, and customer-managed keys. otherwise we want dedicated capacity or a private VPC. we need to understand what 'region lock' means operationally.
[01:33] Diego Alvarez: good question. for Redwood Hosted today we offer region pinning — requests for EU models and inference can be routed to EU hosts; control plane operations can be segregated but we do have a global control plane option. for strict cases we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) where the control plane is customer-managed and data plane stays inside your VPC. note: our Dedicated offering can also be provisioned in a single region with reserved capacity and stronger isolation guarantees.
[02:00] Priya Nair: on the legal side we need to know where logs live and for how long. we also need to know what fields are captured in request/response logs and if we can redact or obfuscate at ingest. e-discovery and audit requests need clear provenance.
[02:15] Diego Alvarez: logging is an area where there's tradeoffs. by default we capture metrics and structured traces for observability, token-level cost breakdowns are also available. but request/response transcript logs are optionally retained and can be configured — you can disable full transcript retention and instead only keep metadata. we also offer redaction hooks and pre-ingest scrubbing.
[02:36] Tom Briggs: what about KV cache — we use a lot of prefix caching and we can't have long term retention that would leak PII. how is that managed?
[02:45] Diego Alvarez: the K V cache (we sometimes call it "K V cash" on transcripts, sorry — the ASR messes that up) is ephemeral per inference session, not persisted long-term unless you enable explicit caching. we can also configure automatic TTLs and encrypt cache keys with your KMS.
[03:03] Sophie Park: encryption — we use an external HSM and keys must never leave our control, does Redwood support customer-managed keys in our HSM?
[03:12] Maya Chen: yes, we support customer-managed keys and BYOK patterns; for Private deployments we can integrate with your on-prem HSM or cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure). for Hosted we support customer KMS integration but some control plane operations may require metadata exchange — that's why many customers pick Dedicated or Private for strict HSM requirements.
[03:35] Alan Rees: audit - we need append-only audit logs with tamper-evidence and exportable S3 archives. retention policy configurable per account. is that in the roadmap or already present?
[03:47] Diego Alvarez: append-only syslogs and audit trails are available on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has audit logs but long-term retention and export is an add-on. we can export to your S3 in EU region and provide r e tention policies; tamper-evidence is part of our audit pipeline (signed log digests).
[04:05] Priya Nair: any certifications? SOC2 yes/no, ISO 27001, HIPAA?
[04:11] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified; we're in progress on ISO 27001 and have a HIPAA implementation guide + BAAs available for enterprise customers. i'll include the artifact pack.
[04:25] Sophie Park: good. another scenario — cross-border fallbacks: if EU capacity is saturated will requests ever cross to US? we cannot allow that.
[04:35] Diego Alvarez: yes we can enforce strict region enforcement policies at the routing layer — you can set hard policy that blocks any fallback outside EU. our SLA would require retry/back-pressure rather than cross-border routing if you enable that. note, that may affect latency during capacity spikes.
[04:55] Tom Briggs: we plan to benchmark latency and token cost. can Redwood provide a test harness and a controlled window where we send synthetic load to both Hosted EU nodes and Dedicated nodes?
[05:06] Diego Alvarez: absolutely, we can set up a one-week benchmark window with telemetry to capture p99 latency, throughput, and cost per token. we'll need your prompt set and expected concurrency.
[05:20] Tom Briggs: will do. question on model variants — if we need a quantized variant for cost reasons, how does Redwood handle model fallbacks and quality regression monitoring?
[05:31] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles and we'll surface quality regression alerts tied to your eval set. rollouts can be canaryed with automatic rollback. SE note: we do quality gating based on chosen metrics.
[05:43] Sophie Park: logging specifics — which headers/fields are considered PII and can we configure field-level redaction?
[05:52] Diego Alvarez: yes, field-level redaction at ingest is supported. we provide a redaction DSL you can configure — regex or structured rules. we also provide a sanitize hook client-side so you can scrub before sending.
[06:06] Priya Nair: for procurement we also need to see contractual limitations on liabilities, data breach procedures, and subprocessor lists.
[06:15] Maya Chen: we'll send a sample DPA and subprocessor list. legal and procurement discussions usually follow pilot success.
[06:25] Alan Rees: do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning? we need RBAC integrated with our directory.
[06:33] Diego Alvarez: yes SAML SSO, OIDC support, and SCIM provisioning for user sync; RBAC is role-based and you can integrate with your IdP.
[06:45] Sophie Park: A follow — can we have a read-only role for auditors that can see audit logs but not request payloads?
[06:52] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can create granular roles; auditors can be given access to finalized audit artifacts but not to raw request data if you prefer.
[07:05] Maya Chen: quick price signal question — what are your cost sensitivity and must-have vs nice-to-have features?
[07:12] Alan Rees: cost is important but not at the expense of compliance. must-haves: EU residency, customer KMS, audit export, RBAC. nice-to-have: model-cost optimization and lower-cost quantized models.
[07:27] Sophie Park: also need a documented incident response flow and contact escalation list for SOC and our infosec.
[07:34] Maya Chen: we'll include an incident response runbook and a dedicated support SLA option.
[07:41] Diego Alvarez: on the technical deep-dive side, we should outline how inference data flows through the stack. do you want us to diagram call flow that shows telemetry vs payload separation?
[07:51] Tom Briggs: yes please, it will help our architecture review board. show where KV cache exists, where prefix caching happens, and where the model weights are stored.
[07:59] Diego Alvarez: note: model weights are separate from request logs; we never persist request payloads into model artifacts.
[08:07] Maya Chen: can we talk about e-discovery and legal holds — how fast can logs be retained/locked on request?
[08:14] Priya Nair: we need a 30-day immediate hold and ability to escalate to a 180-day preservation in special cases.
[08:20] Diego Alvarez: Preservation policies are configurable in Dedicated and Private; hosted can support via add-on. holds can be locked and exports initiated to your archive bucket.
[08:30] Sophie Park: do you allow redaction after the fact or only pre-ingest? sometimes we need to redact after a human review.
[08:37] Diego Alvarez: we support post-ingest redaction workflows, but for compliance we'd recommend pre-ingest scrubbing to minimize exposure. post-ingest requires strict audit and is logged in the tamper-evident trail.
[08:52] Alan Rees: any constraints on throughput for dedicated nodes? we have peak windows with real-time scoring at 300 rps.
[09:01] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated can be sized for predictable throughput; autoscaling with reserved capacity plus burst pools handles spiky workloads. we'll capture your expected seq length distribution and concurrency to size nodes.
[09:12] Tom Briggs: sequence lengths vary a lot. we'll supply token histograms.
[09:18] Maya Chen: great. one blocker we often see is procurement wanting a single-tenant private deployment due to subprocessor rules. what would a Private deployment involve?
[09:29] Diego Alvarez: Private is a customer-managed VPC with a private control plane option, networking controlled by you, optional on-prem package for air-gapped scenarios. it requires longer lead time and an enterprise contract.
[09:42] Sophie Park: what's the expected lead time?
[09:45] Diego Alvarez: Private can be 6-12 weeks depending on custom integrations; Dedicated typically 2-4 weeks to provision. Hosted is immediate but with less control.
[09:56] Priya Nair: also share a list of subprocessors for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. we need to sign off in legal.
[10:03] Maya Chen: will do.
[10:06] Sophie Park: are you able to support region-locked key escrow? we may require key escrow held in EU under a trustee.
[10:14] Diego Alvarez: we have partners who provide key escrow; for Private we can integrate with your escrow provider. for Hosted this is more complex but possible with contractual arrangements.
[10:26] Tom Briggs: about testing — will SE be able to run tests that simulate PII redaction accuracy?
[10:32] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can run redaction accuracy tests and provide false positive/false negative rates against your labeled dataset. we'll include that in the pilot.
[10:44] Maya Chen: just to recap — customer needs: EU-only residency, customer-managed keys, audit exports, RBAC + SSO, configurable retention and redaction, and a pilot in Q1. Redwood will provide SOC2 and HIPAA artifacts, pilot runbook, and a benchmark window. does that capture it?
[11:02] Sophie Park: yes. add contract terms and subprocessors to that list.
[11:08] Priya Nair: procurement timeline — aiming to start pilot approvals by mid-Jan. final production contract by end of Q2.
[11:16] Maya Chen: perfect. next steps — we'll send artifacts and schedule the pilot planning call next week. any final questions?
[11:24] Alan Rees: one more — in the pilot will you allow us to test strict no-fallback region policy?
[11:29] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can enable hard routing policies for the pilot to mimic production constraints.
[11:34] Tom Briggs: i'll share prompts and a token histogram by Friday.
[11:38] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the pack.
[11:42] Sophie Park: thanks everyone.
[11:45] Meeting end.
